sentences.zh: 孝靜世，壬子曆氣朔稍違，熒惑失次，四星出伏，曆亦乖舛。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, the renzi-calendar's qi and new moons gradually diverged; Mars lost its proper stations; the four planets' risings and settings were off; and the calendar too was at variance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing, the renzi calendar's seasonal qi and new moons gradually fell out of alignment; Mars strayed from its stations; the four planets' risings and settings were wrong; and the calendar itself was in error.

sentences.zh: 興和元年十月，齊獻武王入鄴，復命李業興，令其改正，立甲子元曆。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Xinghe, Prince Xianwu of Qi entered Ye, again commissioned Li Yexing, ordered him to correct the calendar, and established the jiazi-origin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Xinghe 1, Prince Xianwu of Qi entered Ye, again commissioned Li Yexing to revise the calendar, and established the jiazi-origin calendar.

sentences.zh: 事訖，尚書左僕射司馬子如、右僕射隆之等表曰：

translations.literal: When the work was finished, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Ziru, Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi, and others memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Ziru, Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi, and others submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 自天地剖判，日月運行，剛柔相摩，寒暑交謝，分之以氣序，紀之以星辰，弦望有盈缺，明晦有修短。

translations.literal: From the separation of Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon have moved; yin and yang have rubbed against each other; cold and heat have succeeded one another. They have been apportioned by the sequence of qi and recorded by the stars and constellations; the new and full moons have waxing and waning, and brightness and darkness have their lengths and brevities.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Heaven and Earth were divided, the sun and moon have run their courses, yin and yang have ground against each other, and cold and heat have given way in turn. The seasons of qi mark their divisions, the stars mark their reckonings, the crescent and full moon know fullness and lack, and light and dark know long and short.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王則之成化，迎日推策，各有司存，以天下之至王，盡生民之能事，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings took this as their model to transform and complete the world. They welcomed the sun and pushed the counting rods; each had his office and charge. As the utmost kings under Heaven, they exhausted what the people could do: acting before Heaven, yet Heaven did not oppose them; acting after Heaven, yet they observed Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old patterned themselves on this to civilize the world. They greeted the sun and advanced the calendar, each with his proper office, and as supreme rulers under Heaven they brought the people's capacities to fulfillment—acting ahead of Heaven without defying it, and acting after Heaven while honoring its seasons.

sentences.zh: 及卯金受命，年曆屢改，當塗啟運，日官變業，分路揚鑣，異門馳騖，回互靡定，交錯不等。

translations.literal: When the Metal Han received the Mandate, the year-calendars were repeatedly changed. When the Tu Wei began its fortune, the officers of the sun changed their methods. They split paths and raised their whips, rushed from different gates, turned and crossed without fixity, and interwove without equality.
translations.idiomatic: When Han received the Mandate, calendars were changed again and again; when Wei rose to power, astronomers altered their methods. Schools went their separate ways, rival traditions raced along, and systems overlapped without ever settling into agreement.

sentences.zh: 豈是人情淺深，苟相違異？

translations.literal: Could this be merely the shallowness or depth of human feeling, carelessly at odds with one another?
translations.idiomatic: Was this merely a matter of scholars' temperaments clashing for no good reason?

sentences.zh: 蓋亦天道盈縮，欲止不能。

translations.literal: Rather, it was also the waxing and waning of the Way of Heaven—wishing to stop yet unable to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, it reflected the ebb and flow of Heaven's way, which cannot be halted even when one wishes to.

sentences.zh: 正光之曆既行於世，發元壬子，置差令朔。

translations.literal: Once the Zhengguang calendar had been put into use in the world, it took its era beginning at renzi and set discrepancies to align the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengguang calendar had come into use, with its era beginning at the renzi year, discrepancies were set so that new moons would fall correctly.

sentences.zh: [1]測影清臺，懸炭之期或爽；

translations.literal: [1] On the Clear Terrace for measuring shadows, the period marked by suspended charcoal at times missed the mark;
translations.idiomatic: [1] Shadow measurements at the Clear Terrace, and the seasons marked by suspended charcoal, sometimes failed to agree;

sentences.zh: 候氣重室，布灰之應少差。

translations.literal: in the layered chamber for observing qi, the response of spread ash showed slight discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: and in the sealed chamber for observing the qi of the seasons, the ash-line responses were slightly off.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下當璧膺符，大橫恊兆，乘機虎變，撫運龍飛，苞括九隅，牢籠萬宇，四海來王，百靈受職。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, bearing the jade disk and receiving the talisman, with great heng and united omens, riding the moment like a tiger's change and nurturing fortune like a dragon's flight, embraces the nine corners and encloses the myriad realms; the four seas come as kings, and the hundred spirits receive their offices.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly observe that Your Majesty has received Heaven's mandate, that great omens unite in your favor, that you seize the moment with tiger-like vigor and ascend with dragon-like fortune, encompassing all corners of the earth and holding the universe in your grasp, while the four seas pay homage and the hundred spirits take their posts.

sentences.zh: 大丞相、勃海王降神挺生，固天縱德，負圖作宰，知機成務，撥亂反正，決江疏河，效顯勤王，勳彰濟世。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, was born when the spirit descended and stood forth; Heaven's virtue was his by nature. He bore the chart and served as chief minister, knew the moment and accomplished affairs, quelled disorder and restored the right, cut through rivers and dredged channels, his merit showing in loyal service to the throne, his achievements shining in succoring the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, was a man of Heaven-sent birth and Heaven-given virtue. Bearing the cosmic chart, he governed as chief minister, seized the right moment to complete great tasks, restored order from chaos, opened rivers and canals, and won renown both for loyal service to the throne and for deeds that saved the world.

sentences.zh: 功成治定，禮樂惟新，以履端歸餘，術數未盡，乃命兼散騎常侍執讀臣李業興，大丞相府東閤祭酒、夷安縣開國公臣王春，大丞相府戶曹參軍臣和貴興等，委其刊正。

translations.literal: When achievements were complete and order settled, rites and music were renewed. Because the beginning of the year and the return of remainders in calendrical reckoning were not yet fully worked out in the arithmetic, he ordered the Concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Reader Li Yexing, the Grand Chancellor's Eastern Pavilion Libationer and Duke of Yi'an Wang Chun, the Grand Chancellor's Household Section Staff Member He Guixing, and others to be entrusted with editing and correcting it.
translations.idiomatic: Once success was won and order restored, rites and music were renewed; yet the calendar's year-beginnings and intercalary remainders were still not fully settled in the computations. He therefore charged Li Yexing, Reader and Concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Wang Chun, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Chancellor's office and Duke of Yi'an, He Guixing, staff member of the Household Section, and others with revising the calendar.

sentences.zh: 但回舍有疾徐，推步有疏密，不可以一方知，難得以一途揆。

translations.literal: Yet in circuit and lodge there are swift and slow phases, and in advancing the steps there are dense and sparse intervals; one cannot know this from a single direction, nor easily measure it by a single path.
translations.idiomatic: Yet orbital circuits have faster and slower phases, and stepwise calculations have tighter and looser intervals; no single method can capture everything, nor can one path alone judge them all.

sentences.zh: 大丞相主簿臣孫搴，驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫臣曄，前給事黃門侍郎臣季景，勃海王世子開府諮議參軍事、定州大中正臣崔暹，業興息國子學生、屯留縣開國子臣子述等，並令參豫，定其是非。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor's Chief Clerk Sun Qian, the General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Ye, the former Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Ji Jing, the Heir of Bohai's Staff Adviser of the Opening Office and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province Cui Xian, Yexing's son the Imperial University student and Baron of Tunliu Zi Shu, and others were all ordered to take part and decide what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, chief clerk to the Grand Chancellor; Ye, General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Ji Jing, former Attendant of the Yellow Gate; Cui Xian, staff adviser to the Heir of Bohai and chief rectifier of Ding Province; Zi Shu, Yexing's son, a student at the Imperial University and Baron of Tunliu; and others were all ordered to join the deliberations and settle disputed points.

sentences.zh: 臣等職司其憂，猶恐未盡。

translations.literal: We, your ministers, hold office charged with this concern, yet still fear it is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: We who hold this office remain anxious that our work may still fall short.

sentences.zh: 竊以蒙戎為飾，必藉眾腋之華；

translations.literal: We venture to think that to trim a coat with fox fur, one must rely on the splendor of many armpit-patches;
translations.idiomatic: We submit that a fur-trimmed robe needs many patches of fine fur to shine;

sentences.zh: 輪奐成宇，寧止一枝之用。

translations.literal: and to complete a hall with splendor, surely more than one beam's use is needed.
translations.idiomatic: and a great hall cannot be built from a single rafter alone.

sentences.zh: 必集名勝，更共修理。

translations.literal: Famous experts must be gathered to revise and repair it together.
translations.idiomatic: We must therefore gather eminent scholars to revise the work together.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫臣盧道約，大司農卿、彭城侯臣李諧，左光祿大夫、東雍州大中正臣裴獻伯，散騎常侍、西兗州大中正臣溫子昇，太尉府長史臣陸操，尚書右丞、城陽縣開國子臣盧元明，中書侍郎臣李同軌，前中書侍郎臣邢子明，中書侍郎臣宇文忠之，前司空府長史、建康伯臣元仲悛，大丞相法曹參軍臣杜弼，尚書左中兵郎中、定陽伯臣李溥濟，尚書起部郎中臣辛術，尚書祠部郎中臣元長和，前青州驃騎府司馬、安定子臣胡世榮，太史令、盧鄉縣開國男臣趙洪慶，太史令臣胡法通，應詔左右臣張喆，員外司馬督臣曹魏祖，太史丞郭慶，太史博士臣胡仲和等，或器標民譽，或術兼世業，並能顯微闡幽，表同錄異，詳考古今，共成此曆。

translations.literal: The Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Lu Daoyue, the Minister of Grand Agriculture and Marquis of Pengcheng Li Xie, the Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Chief Rectifier of Eastern Yong Province Pei Xianbo, the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Chief Rectifier of Western Yan Province Wen Zisheng, the Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant's Office Lu Cao, the Right Assistant of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Chengyang Lu Yuanming, the Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui, the former Secretariat Gentleman Xing Ziming, the Secretariat Gentleman Yuwen Zhongzhi, the former Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works' Office and Baron of Jiankang Yuan Zhongjun, the Grand Chancellor's Legal Section Staff Member Du Bi, the Left Central Troops Bureau Director of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Dingyang Li Puji, the Construction Bureau Director of the Masters of Writing Xin Shu, the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Changhe, the former Chief of Staff of the Agile Cavalry Office of Qing Province and Viscount of Anding Hu Shirong, the Director of the Grand Astrologer and Baron of Luxiang Zhao Hongqing, the Director of the Grand Astrologer Hu Fatong, the Attendant at Imperial Command Zhang Zhe, the Supernumerary Chief of Staff Cao Weizu, the Assistant Director of the Grand Astrologer Guo Qing, the Erudite of the Grand Astrologer Hu Zhonghe, and others—some famed in public reputation, some combining arts with hereditary expertise—all able to display the minute and expound the obscure, set forth what is alike and record what differs, examine ancient and modern in detail, and together complete this calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daoyue, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Li Xie, Minister of Grand Agriculture and Marquis of Pengcheng; Pei Xianbo, Left Grand Master and chief rectifier of Eastern Yong; Wen Zisheng, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of Western Yan; Lu Cao, chief clerk of the Grand Commandant's office; Lu Yuanming, right assistant of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Chengyang; Li Tonggui, Secretariat Gentleman; Xing Ziming, former Secretariat Gentleman; Yuwen Zhongzhi, Secretariat Gentleman; Yuan Zhongjun, former chief clerk of the Minister of Works and Baron of Jiankang; Du Bi, legal-section staff member to the Grand Chancellor; Li Puji, director of the Left Central Troops Bureau and Baron of Dingyang; Xin Shu, Construction Bureau director; Yuan Changhe, Sacrificial Affairs Bureau director; Hu Shirong, former chief of staff of Qing Province's Agile Cavalry office and Viscount of Anding; Zhao Hongqing, Director of the Grand Astrologer and Baron of Luxiang; Hu Fatong, Director of the Grand Astrologer; Zhang Zhe, attendant at imperial command; Cao Weizu, supernumerary chief of staff; Guo Qing, assistant director of the Grand Astrologer; Hu Zhonghe, erudite of the Grand Astrologer; and others—some renowned among the people, some heirs to hereditary expertise—all able to bring out fine points and clarify obscurities, record agreements and differences, scrutinize past and present, and together complete this calendar.

sentences.zh: 甲為日始，子實天正，命曆置元，宜從此起。

translations.literal: Jia is the beginning of days; zi is truly the celestial first month. To set the era beginning of the calendar, one should start from here.
translations.idiomatic: Jia marks the start of the day-cycle, and zi is the true celestial new year; the calendar's era beginning should be established from this point.

sentences.zh: 運屬興和，以年號為目，豈獨太初表於漢代，景初冠於魏曆而已。

translations.literal: Fortune belongs to the Xinghe era; take the reign title as the heading—is this not merely like Taichu being displayed in the Han dynasty and Jingchu crowning the Wei calendar.
translations.idiomatic: As fortune now belongs to the Xinghe era, the reign title should head the calendar—just as Taichu headed Han reckoning and Jingchu crowned Wei's calendar.

sentences.zh: 謹以封呈，乞付有司，依術施用。

translations.literal: We respectfully present this sealed submission and beg that it be handed to the appropriate offices to be applied according to the methods.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully submit this in sealed form and ask that the appropriate offices be ordered to put its methods into practice.

sentences.zh: 詔以新曆示齊獻武王田曹參軍信都芳，芳關通曆術，駁業興曰：「今年十二月二十日，新曆歲星在營室十三度，[2]順，疾；

translations.literal: An edict showed the new calendar to Xin Du Fang, Staff Member of the Fields Section under the Prince of Qi, Xianwu. Fang was versed in calendrical arts and refuted Yexing, saying: "On the twentieth day of the twelfth month this year, the new calendar places Jupiter in Encampment at thirteen degrees, [2] direct, swift;
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the new calendar shown to Xin Du Fang, a staff member in the Fields Section serving Prince Xianwu of Qi. Well versed in calendrical science, Fang challenged Yexing: "On the twentieth day of the twelfth month this year, the new calendar puts Jupiter in Encampment at thirteen degrees, [2] moving direct and fast;

sentences.zh: 天上歲星在營室十一度。

translations.literal: in the sky Jupiter is in Encampment at eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: yet in the sky Jupiter is in Encampment at eleven degrees.

sentences.zh: 今月二十日，新曆鎮星在角十一度，留；

translations.literal: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Saturn in Horn at eleven degrees, stationary;
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Saturn in Horn at eleven degrees, stationary;

sentences.zh: 天上鎮星在亢四度，留。

translations.literal: in the sky Saturn is in Neck at four degrees, stationary.
translations.idiomatic: but in the sky Saturn is in Neck at four degrees, stationary.

sentences.zh: 今月二十日，新曆太白在斗二十五度，晨見，逆行；

translations.literal: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Venus in Dipper at twenty-five degrees, morning appearance, retrograde;
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Venus in Dipper at twenty-five degrees, visible in the morning, retrograde;

sentences.zh: 天上太白在斗二十一度，逆行。

translations.literal: in the sky Venus is in Dipper at twenty-one degrees, retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: yet in the sky Venus is in Dipper at twenty-one degrees, retrograde.

sentences.zh: 便為差殊。」

translations.literal: Thus there are discrepancies."
translations.idiomatic: These are clear discrepancies."

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：

translations.literal: Yexing replied:
translations.idiomatic: Yexing replied:

sentences.zh: 歲星行天，伺候以來八九餘年，恒不及二度。

translations.literal: Jupiter's motion in the heavens, since observations began eight or nine years ago, has constantly fallen short by less than two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Since we began observing Jupiter's course eight or nine years ago, it has consistently lagged by less than two degrees.

sentences.zh: 今新曆加二度。

translations.literal: Now the new calendar adds two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar therefore adds two degrees.

sentences.zh: 至於夕伏晨見，纖毫無爽。

translations.literal: As for evening hiding and morning appearance, there is not the slightest discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: For evening disappearance and morning appearance, there is not the slightest error.

sentences.zh: 今日仰看，如覺二度，及其出沒，還應如術。

translations.literal: Looking up today, it may seem like two degrees, but when it rises and sets, it will still accord with the method.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in the sky today it may look like two degrees off, but at its risings and settings it will still match the computation.

sentences.zh: 鎮星，自造壬子元以來，歲常不及，故加壬子七度，亦知猶不及五度，適欲并加，恐出沒頓校十度、十日，將來永用，不合處多。

translations.literal: Saturn, since the renzi era beginning was devised, each year has constantly fallen short; therefore seven degrees were added to the renzi system, and it is also known that it still falls short by five degrees. Just when one wishes to add them together, one fears that at rising and setting there would suddenly be a correction of ten degrees and ten days; for long-term use in the future there would be many nonconforming points.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn, since the renzi era was established, has year after year lagged behind observation; seven degrees were therefore added to the renzi reckoning, yet it still falls about five degrees short. To add the full amount at once would throw risings and settings off by as much as ten degrees and ten days, and in long use the errors would multiply.

sentences.zh: 太白之行，頓疾頓遲，取其會歸而已。

translations.literal: Venus's motion is now swift, now slow; one takes only its convergent return.
translations.idiomatic: Venus alternates between swift and slow motion; the calendar need only capture its convergent return.

sentences.zh: 近十二月二十日，晨見東方，新舊二曆推之，分寸不異。

translations.literal: Near the twentieth of the twelfth month, at morning appearance in the east, the old and new calendars compute it with not a fraction of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Around the twentieth of the twelfth month, at its morning appearance in the east, old and new calendars agree to the finest fraction.

sentences.zh: 行星三日，頓校四度。

translations.literal: In three days a moving star may suddenly be corrected by four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In three days a planet's position can shift by as much as four degrees.

sentences.zh: 如此之事，無年不有，至其伏見，還依術法。

translations.literal: Matters like this occur every year without exception; when it comes to hiding and appearance, they still follow the computational method.
translations.idiomatic: Such discrepancies occur every year; when planets hide or appear, they still follow the computed rules.

sentences.zh: 又芳唯嫌十二月二十日星有前却。

translations.literal: Moreover, Fang's sole complaint is that on the twentieth of the twelfth month the stars were ahead or behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's complaint, moreover, concerns only the forward or backward discrepancy of the stars on the twentieth of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 業興推步已來，三十餘載，上算千載之日月星辰有見經史者，與涼州趙𢾺、劉義隆廷尉卿何承天、劉駿南徐州從事史祖沖之參校，業興甲子元曆長於三曆一倍。

translations.literal: Since Yexing began advancing the steps, more than thirty years have passed. Computing upward for a thousand years the sun, moon, stars, and planets recorded in the classics and histories, he compared them with Zhao Fei of Liangzhou, He Tiancheng, Minister of Justice under Liu Yilong, and Zu Chongzhi, staff member of Southern Xuzhou under Liu Jun. Yexing's jiazi-era calendar is superior to the three calendars by a full fold.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years Yexing has worked the calendar, checking a millennium of sun, moon, and planetary records in the classics against the systems of Zhao Fei of Liangzhou, He Tiancheng of Liu Song, and Zu Chongzhi—and his jiazi-era calendar outperforms all three by a wide margin.

sentences.zh: 考洛京已來四十餘歲，五星出沒，歲星、鎮星、太白，業興曆首尾恒中，及有差處，不過一日二日、一度兩度；

translations.literal: Examining more than forty years since Luoyang was capital, for the five stars' risings and settings, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus—Yexing's calendar from start to finish has constantly hit the mark; where there are discrepancies, they do not exceed one or two days, one or two degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Over the forty-odd years since Luoyang was capital, for the risings and settings of the five planets—Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus—Yexing's calendar has consistently matched observation; where it errs, the gap is at most a day or two, a degree or two;

sentences.zh: 三曆之失，動校十日十度。

translations.literal: the errors of the three calendars, when checked, often reach ten days and ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: whereas the three rival calendars regularly miss by ten days and ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 熒惑一星，伏見體自無常，或不應度。

translations.literal: Mars alone, in its hiding and appearance, is by nature irregular and sometimes does not match the degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Mars alone is inherently irregular in its appearances and disappearances and sometimes fails to match the predicted degrees.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之曆多甲子曆十日六度，何承天曆不及三十日二十九度；

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi's calendar exceeds the jiazi calendar by ten days and six degrees; He Tiancheng's calendar falls short by twenty-nine days and twenty-nine degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's system runs ten days and six degrees ahead of the jiazi calendar, while He Tiancheng's falls twenty-nine days and twenty-nine degrees behind;

sentences.zh: 今曆還與壬子同，不有加增。

translations.literal: the present calendar still agrees with renzi and has no additions.
translations.idiomatic: the present calendar still follows the renzi reckoning without further adjustment.

sentences.zh: 辰星一星，沒多見少，及其見時，與曆無舛，今此亦依壬子元不改。

translations.literal: Mercury alone hides more and appears less; when it does appear, it is not at odds with the calendar. Here too we follow the renzi era beginning without change.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury hides often and appears rarely; when it does appear, it matches the calendar, and here too we keep the renzi era unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太白、辰星，唯起夕合為異。

translations.literal: For Venus and Mercury, only the evening rising and conjunction differ.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, only evening rising and conjunction present special difficulty.

sentences.zh: 業興以天道高遠，測步難精，五行伏留，推考不易，人目仰窺，未能盡密，但取其見伏大歸，略其中間小謬，如此曆便可行。

translations.literal: Yexing holds that the Way of Heaven is lofty and far; measurement and steps are hard to refine. The five moving stars' hiding and lingering are not easy to compute and examine. Human eyes looking up cannot achieve complete precision. One need only take their great pattern of appearance and hiding and set aside small errors in between—such a calendar can then be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing argues that Heaven's way is vast and observation imperfect; the five planets' stations and retrogradations are hard to compute exactly, and the naked eye cannot catch every detail. One need only capture the broad pattern of their appearances and disappearances and overlook minor mid-course errors—then the calendar is fit for use.

sentences.zh: 若專據所見之驗，不取出沒之效，則曆數之道其幾廢矣。

translations.literal: If one relies solely on what is seen as verification and does not take the effect of rising and setting, then the way of calendrical reckoning would nearly be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If one insisted only on momentary sightings and ignored long-term risings and settings, calendrical science would be all but ruined.

sentences.zh: 夫造曆者，節之與朔貫穿於千年之間，閏餘斗分推之於毫釐之內。

translations.literal: Those who make calendars thread solar terms and new moons through a thousand years and push intercalary remainders and dipper fractions to within hairs and grains.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers must thread solar terms and new moons across a thousand years and push intercalary fractions to within the finest measure.

sentences.zh: 必使盈縮得衷，間限數合，周日小分不殊錙銖，陽曆陰曆纖芥無爽，損益之數驗之交會，日所居度考之月蝕，上推下減，先定眾條，然後曆元可求，猶甲子難值。

translations.literal: They must make waxing and waning hit the mean, interval limits and numbers agree, the circuit day's small fractions differ not by a zhu or shu, solar and lunar calendars miss not by a mustard seed, the numbers of increase and decrease are verified at conjunction, the sun's lodged degree is tested by lunar eclipse, pushing up and reducing down—first fixing the many rules, then the era beginning of the calendar can be sought, yet even jiazi is hard to hit.
translations.idiomatic: Waxing and waning must balance, intervals and constants must align, circuit-day fractions must agree to the smallest unit, solar and lunar reckonings must match exactly, adjustment formulas must check at conjunctions, the sun's position must be tested against eclipses—only after fixing all these rules can the era beginning be found, and even then a jiazi year is hard to land on.

sentences.zh: 又雖值甲子，復有差分，如此踳駁，參錯不等。

translations.literal: Moreover, even when one hits jiazi, there are again fractional discrepancies; thus contradictory and tangled, mixed and unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Even when one reaches a jiazi year, fractional discrepancies remain—systems contradict and fail to align.

sentences.zh: 今曆發元甲子，七率同遵，合璧連珠，其言不失。

translations.literal: The present calendar takes its era beginning at jiazi; the seven rates are uniformly followed; jade disks join and pearls string together—its statements do not fail.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar begins at jiazi, follows seven unified rates, and fits together like joined disks and strung pearls—its claims hold firm.

sentences.zh: 法理分明，情謂為可。

translations.literal: The principles and methods are clear; in our judgment it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Its principles are clear, and we believe it will serve.

sentences.zh: 如芳所言，信亦不謬。

translations.literal: As Fang says, this is indeed not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's observations are not mistaken either.

sentences.zh: 但一合之裏星度不驗者，至若合終必還。

translations.literal: Yet within one conjunction cycle, where star-degrees do not verify, by the end of the conjunction they must return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where degrees fail to match within a single conjunction cycle, they will realign by the cycle's end.

sentences.zh: 依術，鎮星前年十二月二十日見差五度，今日差三度；

translations.literal: By the method, Saturn on the twentieth of the twelfth month two years ago showed a discrepancy of five degrees; today the discrepancy is three degrees;
translations.idiomatic: By computation, Saturn's discrepancy on the twentieth of the twelfth month two years ago was five degrees; today it is three;

sentences.zh: 太白前差四度，今全無差。

translations.literal: Venus formerly differed by four degrees; now there is no discrepancy at all.
translations.idiomatic: Venus formerly differed by four degrees; now there is none at all.

sentences.zh: 以此準之，見伏之驗，尋效可知，將來永用，大體無失。

translations.literal: Measuring by this, verification of appearance and hiding will soon be knowable; for long use in the future, in the main there will be no failure.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this trend, appearances and disappearances will soon prove the method; for long-term use, the calendar will hold in the main.

sentences.zh: 芳又云，以去年十二月中算新曆，其鎮星以十二月二十日在角十一度留，天上在亢四度留，是新曆差天五度；

translations.literal: Fang also said that calculating the new calendar from last year's twelfth month, Saturn on the twentieth of the twelfth month was stationary in Horn at eleven degrees, while in the sky it was stationary in Neck at four degrees—thus the new calendar differed from Heaven by five degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Fang also argued that, reckoning from last December, the new calendar placed Saturn stationary in Horn at eleven degrees on the twentieth, while the sky showed it stationary in Neck at four degrees—a five-degree gap from Heaven;

sentences.zh: 太白、歲星並各有差。

translations.literal: Venus and Jupiter each also had discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Jupiter showed discrepancies as well.

sentences.zh: 校於壬子舊曆，鎮星差天五度，太白歲星亦各有差，是舊曆差天為多，新曆差天為少。

translations.literal: Compared with the old renzi calendar, Saturn differed from Heaven by five degrees, and Venus and Jupiter also each had discrepancies—thus the old calendar's divergence from Heaven was greater, the new calendar's less.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the old renzi calendar, which also missed Saturn by five degrees and Venus and Jupiter by their own margins, the old calendar diverged more from Heaven and the new less.

sentences.zh: 凡造曆者，皆須積年累日，依法候天，知其疏密，然後審其近者，用作曆術。

translations.literal: All who make calendars must accumulate years and pile up days, observe Heaven according to the methods, know what is sparse and dense, and then examine what is nearest and use it as calendrical technique.
translations.idiomatic: Every calendar-maker must observe Heaven year after year, learn where methods are loose or tight, and then adopt the approach that comes closest.

sentences.zh: 不可一月兩月之間，能正是非。

translations.literal: One cannot in the space of one or two months settle right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot settle such questions in a month or two.

sentences.zh: 若如熒惑行天七百七十九日，一遲、一疾、一留、一逆、一順、一伏、一見之法，七頭一終；

translations.literal: For example, Mars traverses the heavens in seven hundred seventy-nine days with one slow, one swift, one stationary, one retrograde, one direct, one hiding, and one appearance—the seven phases completing one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Mars, for instance, completes its cycle in 779 days through seven phases—slow, fast, stationary, retrograde, direct, hidden, and visible—one full round;

sentences.zh: 太白行天五百八十三日，晨夕之法，七頭一終；

translations.literal: Venus traverses the heavens in five hundred eighty-three days with the morning-and-evening method, seven phases one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Venus in 583 days, with its morning-and-evening pattern, seven phases to a cycle;

sentences.zh: 歲星行天三百九十八日，七頭一終；

translations.literal: Jupiter traverses the heavens in three hundred ninety-eight days, seven phases one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter in 398 days, seven phases to a cycle;

sentences.zh: 鎮星行天三百七十八日，七頭一終；

translations.literal: Saturn traverses the heavens in three hundred seventy-eight days, seven phases one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Saturn in 378 days, seven phases to a cycle;

translations.literal: Mercury traverses the heavens in one hundred fifteen days with the morning-and-evening method, seven phases one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury in 115 days, with its morning-and-evening pattern, seven phases to a cycle.

sentences.zh: 造曆者必須測知七頭，然後作術。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers must measure and know the seven phases, and only then devise the methods.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers must observe all seven phases before they can build their methods.

sentences.zh: 得七頭者造曆為近，不得頭者其曆甚疏，皆非一二日能知是非。

translations.literal: Those who obtain the seven phases make calendars that are near; those who do not obtain the phases have calendars that are very sparse—none of these can be judged right or wrong in a day or two.
translations.idiomatic: Those who master the seven phases produce accurate calendars; those who do not produce crude ones—and neither can be judged in a day or two.

sentences.zh: 自五帝三代以來及秦、漢、魏、晉，造曆者皆積年久測，術乃可觀。

translations.literal: From the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties down through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, calendar-makers all accumulated years of long observation before their methods became worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Emperors through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, every sound calendar rested on years of observation.

sentences.zh: 其倉卒造者，當時或近，不可久行。

translations.literal: Those made in haste may at the time be near, but cannot be used for long.
translations.idiomatic: Hastily made calendars may look accurate at first but cannot last.

sentences.zh: 若三四年作者，初雖近天，多載恐失。

translations.literal: If made in three or four years, though at first near Heaven, after many years one fears failure.
translations.idiomatic: Even three- or four-year efforts, though close at first, tend to drift over time.

sentences.zh: 今甲子新曆，業興潛構積年，雖有少差，校於壬子元曆，近天者多。

translations.literal: The present jiazi new calendar was secretly built by Yexing over accumulated years; though there are small discrepancies, compared with the renzi-era calendar it is nearer to Heaven in more respects.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing's new jiazi calendar was built on years of hidden labor; though small errors remain, it matches Heaven more closely than the renzi calendar.

sentences.zh: 若久而驗天，十年二十年間，比壬子元曆，三星行天，其差為密。

translations.literal: If tested against Heaven over a long time, within ten or twenty years compared with the renzi-era calendar, for the three stars' motion in the heavens the discrepancies will be close.
translations.idiomatic: Tested over ten or twenty years against the renzi calendar, the three planets' motions will prove far tighter.

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu reported this upward; an edict ordered it handed outside for implementation.

sentences.zh: 推月朔弦望術第一

translations.literal: Method I: Calculating New Moons, Quarters, and Full Moons
translations.idiomatic: Method I: Calculating New Moons, First and Last Quarters, and Full Moons

sentences.zh: 推積月術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以章月乘之，章歲如一，所得為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated months: Set [the count] from entering the cycle through the year sought in full, subtract one; multiply by rule-months; as rule-years yields one—what is obtained is accumulated months; what does not exhaust is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find accumulated months: take all years from cycle entry through the target year, subtract one; multiply by rule-months (6,951) and divide by rule-years (562); the quotient is accumulated months, the remainder the leap fraction.

sentences.zh: 閏餘三百五十五以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is 355 or above, that year has an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: A leap month occurs when the intercalary remainder reaches 355 or higher.

sentences.zh: 餘五百一十五以上，進退在天正十一月前後，以冬至定之。

translations.literal: If the remainder is 515 or above, advance or retreat before or after the Heavenly First eleventh month—determine by Winter Solstice.
translations.idiomatic: When the remainder is 515 or more, adjust placement before or after the civil eleventh month according to where Winter Solstice falls.

sentences.zh: 推積日術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分，日法如一，為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated days: Multiply accumulated months by the communication number for the new-moon accumulated fraction; as the day divisor yields one, that is accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find accumulated days: multiply accumulated months by the communication number (6,158,017), divide by the day divisor (208,530); the quotient is accumulated days, the residue the minor remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce accumulated days modulo sixty; the remainder is the large remainder.

sentences.zh: 命大餘以紀，

translations.literal: Count the large remainder by the cycle,
translations.idiomatic: Index the large remainder against the cycle,

sentences.zh: 〈今命以甲戌紀。〉

translations.literal: 〈Now count by the jiaxu cycle.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈At present count from the jiaxu cycle.〉

sentences.zh: 算外，即所求年天正十一月朔日。

translations.literal: outside the reckoning: the new-moon day of the Heavenly First eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: then step one past the count: the new moon of the eleventh civil month in the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次月朔術曰：加大餘二十九、小餘十一萬六百四十七，滿除如上，命以紀，算外，即次月朔日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month's new moon: Add to the large remainder twenty-nine and to the small remainder 110,647; when full, reduce as above; count by the cycle; outside the reckoning—that is the next month's new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following new moon add 29 to the large remainder and 110,647 to the small remainder, carrying overflows as before; index against the cycle and step past the count for the next conjunction date.

sentences.zh: 其小餘滿虛分九萬七千八百八十三者，其月大；

translations.literal: When the small remainder fills the void fraction 97,883, that month is long;
translations.idiomatic: If the minor remainder reaches the void fraction (97,883), the month is long (thirty days);

sentences.zh: 減者，其月小。

translations.literal: when reduced, that month is short.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise it is short (twenty-nine days).

sentences.zh: 求上下弦望術曰：加朔大餘七、小餘七萬九千七百九十四、小分一。

translations.literal: Method for seeking first quarter, full moon, and last quarter: Add to the new-moon large remainder seven, to the small remainder 79,794, and one minor part.
translations.idiomatic: To find the upper quarter, full moon, and lower quarter: add 7 to the large remainder, 79,794 to the small remainder, and 1 minor part.

sentences.zh: 小分滿四，從小餘；

translations.literal: When minor parts fill four, carry to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: Carry at four minor parts into the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿日法，從大餘；

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder;
translations.idiomatic: carry at the day divisor into the large remainder;

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十，去之，命以紀，算外，即上弦日。

translations.literal: when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; count by the cycle; outside the reckoning, [14] that is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: reduce the large remainder modulo sixty, index against the cycle, and step past the count [14] for the first-quarter date.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月朔。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition to reach full moon, last quarter, and the following new moon.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣閏術第二

translations.literal: Method II: The Twenty-Four Qi and Intercalation
translations.idiomatic: Method II: Calculating the Twenty-Four Solar Terms and Intercalary Months

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以餘數乘之，蔀法如一，為積沒，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the twenty-four qi: Set [the count] from entering the cycle through the year sought in full, subtract one; multiply by the remainder number; as the obscuration divisor yields one, that is accumulated submergence; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the twenty-four solar terms: take all years from cycle entry through the target year, subtract one; multiply by the remainder number (88,417) and divide by the obscuration divisor (16,860); the quotient is accumulated submergence, the residue the minor remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至日。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated submergence; what does not exhaust is the large remainder; count by the cycle; outside the reckoning: the Winter Solstice day of the Heavenly First eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce modulo sixty for the large remainder, index against the cycle, and step past the count for the Winter Solstice of the eleventh civil month in the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次氣術術曰：加大餘十五、小餘三千六百八十四、小分一，小分滿小分法二十四，從小餘；

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next qi says: Add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder 3,684, and one minor part; when minor parts fill the minor-part divisor twenty-four, carry to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: For the next solar term add 15 to the large remainder, 3,684 to the small remainder, and 1 minor part; carry at twenty-four minor parts into the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿蔀法，從大餘一，命如上，[15]算外，即次氣日。

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry one to the large remainder; count as above; [15] outside the reckoning: the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: carry at the obscuration divisor into the large remainder, index as before, and step past the count [15] for the next term's date.

sentences.zh: 推閏術曰：以閏餘減章歲，餘以歲中十二乘之，滿章閏二百七得一，月餘半法以上亦得一月，數起天正十一月，算外，即閏月。

translations.literal: Method for pushing intercalation: Subtract the intercalary remainder from rule-years; multiply the remainder by mid-year qi twelve; when it fills rule intercalations 207 obtain one; when the monthly remainder is half the divisor or above, also obtain one month; count from the Heavenly First eleventh month; outside the reckoning: the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: For the leap month: subtract the leap fraction from rule-years (562); multiply the result by twelve and divide by rule intercalations (207); add another month if the monthly remainder reaches half the divisor; count forward from the civil eleventh month and step past the count to name the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 閏月有進退，[16]以無中氣定之。

translations.literal: The intercalary month may advance or retreat; [16] determine it by the absence of a mid-climate.
translations.idiomatic: Placement of the leap month may shift; [16] fix it by which month lacks a mid-climate.

sentences.zh: 推閏又法術曰：以歲中乘閏餘，如章閏得一，[17]盈章中六千七百四十四，數起冬至，算外，中氣終閏月也。

translations.literal: Alternate method for pushing intercalation: Multiply the intercalary remainder by mid-year qi; as rule intercalations yields one, [17] when it fills rule mid-climates 6,744, count from Winter Solstice; outside the reckoning: the mid-climate ends and the intercalary month [follows].
translations.idiomatic: Alternate leap-month procedure: multiply the leap fraction by twelve and divide by rule intercalations (207); [17] when the product exceeds rule mid-climates (6,744), count from Winter Solstice and step past the count—where a mid-climate ends, place the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 盈中氣在朔若二日，即前月閏。

translations.literal: If the mid-climate excess falls on the new moon or the second day, then the preceding month is intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: When the overflow mid-climate falls on the conjunction day or the day after, the previous month is the leap month.

sentences.zh: 不盡者，以日法約之，為度，不盡者為度餘，即所求年天正十一月朔却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: what does not exhaust, reduce by the day divisor for degrees; what does not exhaust is the degree remainder: the degrees and degree remainder by which the Heavenly First eleventh-month new moon of the year sought stands back from the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder, divided by the day divisor, gives degrees and a degree remainder—the node distance for the eleventh-month new moon of the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次月却去交度術曰：加度二十九、度餘十一萬六百四十七，度餘滿日法從度，度滿會數去之，亦除其會餘，即次月朔却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month's degrees back from the crossing says: Add 29 degrees and degree remainder 110,647; when the degree remainder fills the day divisor, carry to degrees; when degrees fill the conjunction number, remove it and also eliminate the conjunction remainder—the degrees and degree remainder by which the next month's new moon stands back from the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: For the next month: add 29° and remainder 110,647; carry remainder into degrees at the day divisor, drop full conjunction cycles from degrees, and trim the conjunction remainder—the result is the nodal distance for the following new moon.

sentences.zh: 求望却去交度術曰：加度十四、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半，滿除如上，即望却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the full moon's degrees back from the crossing says: Add 14 degrees and degree remainder 159,588½; when full, eliminate as above—the degrees and degree remainder by which the full moon stands back from the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: For the full moon add 14° and remainder 159,588½ and apply the same carry-and-reduce rules to obtain its nodal distance.

sentences.zh: 推月在日道表裏術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以紀交會差分并之，倍會通去之，餘以會通減之，得一減者，為月在日道裏；

translations.literal: Method for pushing whether the moon is on the outer or inner side of the solar path says: Set the new-moon accumulated fraction from entering the cycle, add the cycle conjunction-difference fraction, remove double conjunction communication, subtract the remainder from conjunction communication; when one subtraction is obtained, the moon is on the inner side of the solar path;
translations.idiomatic: To place the moon north or south of the ecliptic: take accumulated new-moon parts from cycle entry, add the cycle's conjunction-difference fraction, divide by twice the conjunction communication, and subtract the remainder from one full conjunction communication—a single subtraction means the moon is south of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 無所得者，為月在日道表。

translations.literal: when none is obtained, the moon is on the outer side of the solar path.
translations.idiomatic: no subtraction means the moon is north of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 求次月表裏術曰：加次月度及度餘，加表滿會數及會數餘，則在裏；

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month's outer or inner side says: Add the next month's degrees and degree remainder; when on the outer side and it fills the conjunction number and conjunction-number remainder, then it is on the inner side;
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add the tabulated degree increment; when starting from the outer track, filling the conjunction number and its remainder switches the moon to the inner track;

sentences.zh: 加裏滿會數及會餘，則在表。

translations.literal: when on the inner side and it fills the conjunction number and conjunction remainder, then it is on the outer side.
translations.idiomatic: from the inner track, the same overflow places it back on the outer track.

sentences.zh: 推交道所在日術曰：以十一月朔却去交度及餘減會數及會餘，會餘若不足減者，減一度，加日法乃減之；

translations.literal: Method for pushing the day on which the crossing-way lies says: Subtract the eleventh-month new moon's degrees and remainder back from the crossing from the conjunction number and conjunction remainder; if the conjunction remainder is insufficient to subtract, reduce one degree and add the day divisor before subtracting;
translations.idiomatic: To find the day of nodal passage: subtract the November new moon's nodal distance from the conjunction number and remainder; if the remainder is too small, borrow one degree and add the day divisor before subtracting;

sentences.zh: 又以十一月朔小餘加之，滿日法從度，餘為度餘，即是天正十一月朔前去交度及餘。

translations.literal: further add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; when it fills the day divisor, carry to degrees; the remainder is the degree remainder—this is the degrees and remainder before the Heavenly First eleventh-month new moon from the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: add the November syzygy's fine fraction; carry at the day divisor into degrees—the remainder gives the nodal arc elapsed before civil-year November conjunction.

sentences.zh: 如曆月大小除之，起天正月十一月，不滿月者為入月，算外，交道所在日。

translations.literal: eliminate per the calendar's long and short months, starting from Heavenly First month eleven; what does not fill a month is the entered month; outside the reckoning: the day on which the crossing-way lies.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by successive month lengths from civil month 11; the fractional month is months entered; step past the count to name the day of nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 又以歲中乘入月小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外，[19]即交道所在辰。

translations.literal: further multiply the entered month's small remainder by mid-year qi, divide by the day divisor; what is obtained, count from zi; outside the reckoning, [19] the double-hour in which the crossing-way lies.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the entered month's fine parts by twelve and divide by the day divisor; count the quotient from zi and step past the count [19] for the double-hour of the crossing.

sentences.zh: 其交在望前者，其月朔則交會，[20]望則月蝕。

translations.literal: When the crossing is before the full moon, that month at new moon there is conjunction-crossing, [20] at full moon there is lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If the node precedes full moon, that month has a solar eclipse at conjunction [20] and a lunar eclipse at full moon.

sentences.zh: 交在望後者，其月月蝕，後朔交會。

translations.literal: When the crossing is after the full moon, that month there is lunar eclipse, and at the following new moon conjunction-crossing.
translations.idiomatic: If the node follows full moon, the month has a lunar eclipse first and solar eclipse at the next syzygy.

sentences.zh: 交正在望者，其月月蝕既，前後朔交會。

translations.literal: When the crossing is exactly at the full moon, that month the lunar eclipse is total, and at the preceding and following new moons conjunction-crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the node aligns with full moon, a total lunar eclipse occurs, with solar eclipses at the adjacent new moons.

sentences.zh: 交正朔者，日蝕既，前後月望皆月蝕。

translations.literal: When the crossing is exactly at new moon, the solar eclipse is total, and the full moons of the preceding and following months are both lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: With the node on conjunction day, a total solar eclipse; the full moons before and after both yield lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 求後交月及日術曰：以會數及會餘加前入月算及餘，餘滿日法從日，日如曆月大小除之，起前交月，算外，即後交月及日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the later crossing month and day says: Add the conjunction number and conjunction remainder to the prior entered-month count and remainder; when the remainder fills the day divisor, carry to days; eliminate days per the calendar's long and short months, starting from the prior crossing month; outside the reckoning: the later crossing month and day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next crossing: add the conjunction number and remainder to the prior month count and fraction; carry at the day divisor, divide by month lengths from the previous crossing month, and step past the count for the next crossing date.

sentences.zh: 以次放之。

translations.literal: Extend by this pattern in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same steps for each subsequent crossing.

sentences.zh: 推交會起角術曰：其月在外道，先會後交者，虧從東南角起；

translations.literal: Method for pushing the starting horn of conjunction-crossing says: When the month is on the outer path, if conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the southeast horn;
translations.idiomatic: To find the eclipse quadrant: on the outer track, if syzygy precedes the node, the bite begins at the southeast limb;

sentences.zh: 先交後會者，虧從西南角起。

translations.literal: if crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the southwest horn.
translations.idiomatic: if the node precedes syzygy, the bite begins at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 其月在內道，先會後交者，虧從西北角起，合交中者，蝕之既。

translations.literal: When the month is on the inner path, if conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the northwest horn; when crossing meets center, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: On the inner track, syzygy before the node starts the bite at the northwest limb; a central crossing yields a total eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕在日之衝，起角亦如之。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse at the sun's opposite, the starting horn is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipses at opposition, apply the same quadrant rule.

sentences.zh: 推蝕分多少術曰：其朔望去交度及度餘如入交限數一百五十八度、度餘十一萬六千五十八半以上者，以減會數及會數餘，餘為不蝕度。

translations.literal: Method for pushing how great or small the eclipse fraction is says: If the new or full moon's degrees and degree remainder back from the crossing are like the entering-crossing limit of 158 degrees and degree remainder 116,058½ or above, subtract from the conjunction number and conjunction-number remainder; the remainder is the non-eclipse degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For eclipse magnitude: if the syzygy's nodal distance reaches the entering limit (158°; remainder 116,058½) or more, subtract from the conjunction number and remainder—the remainder is the non-eclipse arc.

sentences.zh: 若朔望去交度如朔望合數十四度、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半以下者，即是不蝕度。

translations.literal: If the new or full moon's degrees back from the crossing are like the new-full conjunction number of 14 degrees and degree remainder 159,588½ or below, that is the non-eclipse degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If the nodal distance is at or below the syzygy conjunction number (14°; remainder 159,588½), there is no eclipse.

sentences.zh: [21]皆以減十五，餘為蝕分。

translations.literal: [21] In each case subtract from fifteen; the remainder is the eclipse fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [21] Subtract each case from 15; the remainder is the eclipse magnitude in fifteenths.

sentences.zh: [22]朔望去交度盡者，蝕之既。

translations.literal: [22] When the new or full moon's degrees back from the crossing are exhausted, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: [22] When the nodal distance is zero, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月蝕入遲疾曆盈縮術第四

translations.literal: Method IV: Pushing Conjunction and Lunar Eclipse Entry into the Slow-Fast Ephemeris, Surplus and Shrinkage

sentences.zh: 推合朔入遲疾曆術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以所入紀遲疾差分并之，

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction entry into the slow-fast ephemeris says: Set the new-moon accumulated fraction from entering the cycle, and add the slow-fast difference fraction of the cycle entered,
translations.idiomatic: To place a syzygy in the lunar anomaly table: take accumulated new-moon parts from cycle entry and add the slow-fast difference fraction for the current cycle,

translations.idiomatic: 〈For the jiaxu cycle the slow-fast difference fraction is 2,352,191.〉

sentences.zh: [23]以通周去之，所得為積周；

translations.literal: [23] remove by communication cycles; what is obtained is accumulated cycles;
translations.idiomatic: [23] divide by communication cycles; the quotient is accumulated cycles;

sentences.zh: [24]不盡者，以日法約之，為日，不盡者為日餘。

translations.literal: [24] what does not exhaust, reduce by the day divisor for days; what does not exhaust is the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: [24] the remainder, divided by the day divisor, gives whole days and a day remainder.

sentences.zh: 命日，算外，即所求年天正月十一月合朔入曆日。

translations.literal: Count the day; outside the reckoning: the day on which the Heavenly First eleventh-month conjunction of the year sought enters the ephemeris.
translations.idiomatic: Index the day and step past the count for the anomaly-table day of the target year's civil November conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求次月入曆日術曰：加一日、日餘二十萬三千五百四十六，日蝕滿日法從日，[25]日滿周日及周餘去之，命如上，算外，即次月入曆日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month's entry day says: Add one day and day remainder 203,546; when the day eclipse fills the day divisor, carry to the day; [25] when the day fills the circuit week and week remainder, remove them; count as above; outside the reckoning: the next month's entry day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 1 day and remainder 203,546; carry remainder into days at the day divisor; [25] drop full circuit weeks; index as before to obtain the next entry day.

sentences.zh: 月蝕者，隨定大小餘為定日加時。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse, follow the fixed great and small remainders [40] as the fixed day addition hour.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipse, take the fixed great and small remainders [40] as the true time of day.

sentences.zh: 推加時術曰：以歲中乘定小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the addition hour says: Multiply the fixed small remainder by year medial [parts], divide by the day divisor; count the result from zi; outside the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: To find the hour of occurrence: multiply the fixed small remainder by 12 (year medial) and divide by the day divisor; index from zi and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 朔望加時有餘不盡者，四之，如法得一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: When the new- or full-moon addition hour has a remainder not exhausted, quadruple it; per divisor 1 is shao, 2 is ban, 3 is tai.
translations.idiomatic: For a fractional hour at syzygy, quadruple the remainder: 1/4 of the divisor is shao, 2/4 is ban, 3/4 is tai.

sentences.zh: 半又有餘者，三之，如法得一為強，半法以上排成一，不滿半法棄之。

translations.literal: When the half still has remainder, triple it; per divisor 1 is qiang; at half the divisor and above round up to one; below half the divisor discard.
translations.idiomatic: If the half-degree still has remainder, triple it: one third of the divisor is qiang; at half the divisor or more round up, otherwise discard.

sentences.zh: 以強并少為少強，并半為半強，并太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao for shao-qiang, with ban for ban-qiang, with tai for tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add qiang to shao for shao-qiang, to ban for ban-qiang, to tai for tai-qiang.

sentences.zh: 得二強者為少弱，以之并少為半弱，以之并半為太弱，以之并太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: When two qiang are obtained, it is shao-ruo; combine with shao for ban-ruo, with ban for tai-ruo, with tai for one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two qiang yield shao-ruo; added to shao gives ban-ruo, to ban gives tai-ruo, to tai gives one full lodge-ruo.

sentences.zh: 隨所在辰而命之，即其強弱。

translations.literal: Name according to the lodge where it stands—that is its strength or weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Name the lodge reached—that is the strength grade.

sentences.zh: 日之衝為破，月常在破下蝕。

translations.literal: The sun's opposite is po; the moon is always eclipsed below po.
translations.idiomatic: The sun’s opposition point is po; eclipses occur when the moon stands there.

sentences.zh: 推日月合朔弦望度術第五[41] 推日度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以日度法一萬六千八百六十乘之，滿周天去之，餘以日度法約之為度，不盡為餘。

translations.literal: Method V: Pushing Sun and Moon Conjunction, New Moon, Quarter, and Full Moon Degrees [41]. Method for pushing solar degree says: Set accumulated new-moon days from entering the cycle; multiply by the solar-degree divisor 16,860; when it fills the circuit of heaven, remove it; reduce the remainder by the solar-degree divisor for degrees; what does not exhaust is the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Method V: Syzygy and Lunar Phase Longitudes [41]. Solar longitude: set accumulated new-moon days from cycle entry, multiply by solar-degree divisor 16,860, remove full circuits of heaven, and reduce the remainder to degrees and a remainder.

sentences.zh: [42]命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。

translations.literal: [42] Count from twelve degrees before Ox; eliminate by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—outside the reckoning: the degree and parts where the sun stands at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: [42] Index from 12° before Ox, walk through the lodges, and step past the count—the remainder is the sun’s midnight longitude at civil-year November new moon.

sentences.zh: 推日度又法，術曰：置周天三百六十五度、斗分四千一百一十七，以冬至去朔日數減一，以減周天度，冬至小餘減斗分；

translations.literal: Alternate method for pushing solar degree says: Set the circuit of heaven 365 degrees and Dipper fraction 4,117; subtract one from the number of days from winter solstice to new moon, and subtract that from circuit-of-heaven degrees; subtract the winter-solstice small remainder from the Dipper fraction;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate solar-longitude method: set 365° plus Dipper fraction 4,117, subtract (days from winter solstice to new moon − 1) from the circuit, and subtract the winter-solstice small remainder from the Dipper fraction;

sentences.zh: 斗分不足減者，減一度，加日度法乃減之。

translations.literal: when the Dipper fraction is insufficient to subtract, reduce one degree and add the solar-degree divisor before subtracting.
translations.idiomatic: if the Dipper fraction is too small, borrow 1° and add the solar-degree divisor, then subtract.

sentences.zh: 命起如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。

translations.literal: Count as above; outside the reckoning: the degree and parts where the sun stands at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Index as before and step past the count for the sun’s midnight longitude at civil-year November new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月次日日所在度[43]術曰：月大者加度三十，月小者加度二十九，次日者加度一，宿次除之，逕斗除其分。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month’s and next day’s solar positions [43] says: For a long month add 30 degrees; for a short month add 29; for the next day add 1 degree; eliminate by lodge sequence; pass Dipper and remove its fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For later days [43]: add 30° in a long month, 29° in a short month, 1° for the next day; walk the lodges and deduct the Dipper fraction.
