sentences.zh: 推合朔日月共度術曰：以章歲五百六十二乘朔小餘，以章月六千九百五十一除之，所得為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction solar-lunar shared degree says: Multiply the new-moon small remainder by Rule Years 562; divide by Rule Months 6,951; what is obtained is the great fraction; what does not exhaust is the small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Shared syzygy longitude: multiply the new-moon small remainder by rule years 562 and divide by rule months 6,951 for great and small fractions.

sentences.zh: 以加夜半日度分，分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: Add to midnight solar degree and fraction; when the fraction fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; count as above; outside the reckoning: the shared solar-lunar degree at conjunction for civil-year November new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Add to midnight solar longitude, carry at the solar-degree divisor, index the lodges, and step past the count for November syzygy longitude.

sentences.zh: 推合朔日月共度又法，術曰：加度二十九、大分八千九百四十五、小分六千九百一十九，小分滿章月從大分；

translations.literal: Alternate method for shared conjunction degree says: Add 29 degrees, great fraction 8,945, and small fraction 6,919; when the small fraction fills Rule Months, carry to the great fraction;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate syzygy longitude: add 29°, great fraction 8,945, and small fraction 6,919; carry small to great at rule months;

sentences.zh: 大分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，逕斗去其分，算外，即次月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: when the great fraction fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; eliminate by lodge sequence; pass Dipper and remove its fraction; outside the reckoning: the next month’s shared conjunction degree.
translations.idiomatic: carry great to degrees at the solar-degree divisor, walk the lodges, deduct the Dipper fraction, and step past the count for the next month’s syzygy longitude.

sentences.zh: 推月度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以月周二十二萬五千三百九十乘之，[45]滿周天去之。

translations.literal: Method for pushing lunar degree says: Set accumulated new-moon days from entering the cycle; multiply by Lunar Circumference 225,390; [45] when it fills the circuit of heaven, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar longitude: set accumulated new-moon days from cycle entry, multiply by lunar circuit 225,390, [45] and remove full circuits of heaven.

sentences.zh: 餘以日度法約之為度，餘為度分，命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Reduce the remainder by the solar-degree divisor for degrees; the remainder is degree fraction; count from twelve degrees before Ox; eliminate by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—outside the reckoning: the degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce to degrees and fractional parts, index from 12° before Ox, walk the lodges, and step past the count for the moon’s midnight longitude at November new moon.

sentences.zh: 推月度又法，術曰：以小周乘朔小餘為實，章歲乘日法為法，實如法得一為度；

translations.literal: Alternate method for lunar degree says: Multiply the new-moon small remainder by Lesser Circumference for the dividend; multiply Rule Years by the day divisor for the divisor; the dividend per divisor is one degree;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate lunar longitude: Lesser Zhou × new-moon small remainder over rule years × day divisor gives degrees;

sentences.zh: 不滿法者，以章月除之為大分，餘為小分。

translations.literal: what does not fill the divisor, divide by Rule Months for the great fraction; the remainder is the small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder divides by rule months for great fraction, with the residue as small fraction.

sentences.zh: 所得以減合朔度及度分，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Subtract what is obtained from the conjunction degree and degree fraction; outside the reckoning: the degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from syzygy longitude and step past the count for the moon’s midnight position at November new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月月度術[46]曰：月小，加度二十二、分七千三百七十三，月大，加度三十五、分一萬三千五百八十三，分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即月次月所在度。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month’s lunar degree [46] says: In a short month add 22 degrees and fraction 7,373; in a long month add 35 degrees and fraction 13,583; when the fraction fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; eliminate by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—outside the reckoning: the moon’s degree in the next month.
translations.idiomatic: Next month’s moon [46]: add 22° and fraction 7,373 in a short month or 35° and fraction 13,583 in a long month, carry at the solar-degree divisor, walk the lodges, and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 求次日月度術[47]曰：加度十三、分六千二百一十，分滿日度法從度，除如上，算外，即月次日所在度。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next day’s lunar degree [47] says: Add 13 degrees and fraction 6,210; when the fraction fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; eliminate as above; outside the reckoning: the moon’s degree on the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Next day’s moon [47]: add 13° and fraction 6,210, carry, walk the lodges, and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 求弦望日所在度術曰：加合朔度七、大分六千四百五十一、小分三千四百六十七、[48]微分二，微分滿四從小分，小分滿章月從大分，大分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即上弦日所在度。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the degree where the sun stands at first and last quarter says: Add to the conjunction degree 7, great fraction 6,451, small fraction 3,467, and minute fraction 2; when minute fractions fill four, carry to small fraction; when small fraction fills Rule Months, carry to great fraction; when great fraction fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; count as above; outside the reckoning: the sun’s degree at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: First-quarter sun: add 7°, great fraction 6,451, small fraction 3,467, and minute fraction 2 to syzygy longitude with the usual carries, then index the lodges for first-quarter solar longitude.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、[49]下弦、後月合朔。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month’s conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same increment for full moon, last quarter, and the next syzygy.

sentences.zh: 求弦望月所在度術曰：加合朔度九十八、大分一萬一千六百九十五、小分五千二百二十五、微分一，滿除如上，算外，即上弦日月所在度。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the degree where the moon stands at first and last quarter says: Add to the conjunction degree 98, great fraction 11,695, small fraction 5,225, and minute fraction 1; when full, eliminate as above; outside the reckoning: the shared sun-and-moon degree at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: First-quarter moon: add 98°, great fraction 11,695, small fraction 5,225, and minute fraction 1 to syzygy longitude with the usual carries for first-quarter lunar longitude.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月合朔。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month’s conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat for full moon, last quarter, and the next syzygy.

sentences.zh: 斗二十六度 牛八度 女十二度 虛十度

translations.literal: Dipper 26 degrees; Ox 8 degrees; Maid 12 degrees; Void 10 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Dipper 26°; Ox 8°; Maid 12°; Void 10°

sentences.zh: 危十七度 室十六度 壁九度

translations.literal: Rooftop 17 degrees; Encampment 16 degrees; Wall 9 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Rooftop 17°; Encampment 16°; Wall 9°

sentences.zh: 北方玄武七宿：九十八度分四千一百一十七

translations.literal: Northern Dark Warrior seven lodges: 98 degrees, fraction 4,117
translations.idiomatic: Northern Dark Warrior (seven lodges): 98°; fraction 4,117

sentences.zh: 奎十六度 婁十二度 胃十四度 昴十一度

translations.literal: Legs 16 degrees; Bond 12 degrees; Stomach 14 degrees; Hairy Head 11 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Legs 16°; Bond 12°; Stomach 14°; Hairy Head 11°

sentences.zh: 畢十六度 觜二度 參九度

translations.literal: Net 16 degrees; Turtle Beak 2 degrees; Three Stars 9 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Net 16°; Turtle Beak 2°; Three Stars 9°

sentences.zh: 西方白虎七宿：八十度

translations.literal: Western White Tiger seven lodges: 80 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Western White Tiger (seven lodges): 80°

sentences.zh: 井三十三度 鬼四度 柳十五度 星七度

translations.literal: Well 33 degrees; Ghost 4 degrees; Willow 15 degrees; Star 7 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Well 33°; Ghost 4°; Willow 15°; Star 7°

sentences.zh: 張十八度 翼十八度 軫十七度

translations.literal: Spread 18 degrees; Wings 18 degrees; Chariot Shaft 17 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Spread 18°; Wings 18°; Chariot Shaft 17°

sentences.zh: 南方朱鳥七宿：一百一十二度

translations.literal: Southern Vermilion Bird seven lodges: 112 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Southern Vermilion Bird (seven lodges): 112°

sentences.zh: 角十二度 亢九度 氐十五度 房五度

translations.literal: Horn 12 degrees; Neck 9 degrees; Root 15 degrees; Chamber 5 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Horn 12°; Neck 9°; Root 15°; Chamber 5°

sentences.zh: 心五度 尾十八度 箕十一度

translations.literal: Heart 5 degrees; Tail 18 degrees; Winnowing Basket 11 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Heart 5°; Tail 18°; Winnowing Basket 11°

sentences.zh: 東方倉龍七宿：七十五度

translations.literal: Eastern Azure Dragon seven lodges: 75 degrees
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Azure Dragon (seven lodges): 75°

sentences.zh: 周天三百六十五度、一萬六千八百六十分度之四千一百一十七，通之，得六百一十五萬八千一十七，名曰周天。

translations.literal: Circuit of heaven 365 degrees and 4,117 parts of 16,860 parts per degree—combined, 6,158,017; named Circuit of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit of heaven: 365° plus 4,117/16,860 per degree—combined total 6,158,017, called the circuit of heaven.

sentences.zh: 推土王滅沒卦候上朔術第六

translations.literal: Method VI: Pushing Earth King, Extinction and Submersion, Hexagrams, Pitch-Pipes, and Upper New Moon
translations.idiomatic: Method VI: Earth-King Days, Extinction and Submersion, Hexagrams, Pitch-Pipes, and Upper Syzygy

sentences.zh: 推土王日術曰：置四立大小餘，各減其大餘十八、小餘四千四百二十、小分十八、微分二，大餘不足減者，加六十乃減之；

translations.literal: Method for pushing Earth King days says: Set the great and small remainders of the four establishments; from each subtract great remainder 18, small remainder 4,420, small fraction 18, and minute fraction 2; when great remainder is insufficient, add 60 before subtracting;
translations.idiomatic: Earth-king days: take the four establishment remainders and subtract great remainder 18, small remainder 4,420, small fraction 18, and minute fraction 2; borrow 60 for the great remainder if needed;

sentences.zh: 小餘不足減者，減一日，加蔀法乃減之；

translations.literal: when small remainder is insufficient, subtract one day and add the Obscuration divisor before subtracting;
translations.idiomatic: borrow one day and add the obscuration divisor for the small remainder if needed;

sentences.zh: 小分不足減者，減小餘一，加小分法二十四乃減之；

translations.literal: when small fraction is insufficient, subtract one small remainder and add 24 of the small-fraction divisor before subtracting;
translations.idiomatic: borrow one small remainder and add 24 small-fraction parts if needed;

sentences.zh: 微分不足減者，減小分一，加五，然後皆減之。

translations.literal: when minute fraction is insufficient, subtract one small fraction and add five, then subtract all.
translations.idiomatic: borrow one small fraction and add five minute parts, then complete the subtraction.

sentences.zh: 命以紀，算外，即四立前土王日。

translations.literal: Count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the Earth King day before each of the four establishments.
translations.idiomatic: Index by cycle and step past the count for the earth-king day before each establishment.

sentences.zh: 推土王又法，術曰：加冬至大餘二十七、小餘六千六百三十一、小分六、微分三，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘一，命以紀，算外，即季冬土王日。

translations.literal: Alternate method for Earth King says: Add to winter solstice great remainder 27, small remainder 6,631, small fraction 6, and minute fraction 3; when minute fractions fill five, carry to small fraction; when small fraction fills the small-fraction divisor, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the Obscuration divisor, carry one to great remainder; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the Earth King day of late winter.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate earth-king method: add to winter solstice great remainder 27, small remainder 6,631, small fraction 6, and minute fraction 3 with the usual carries, index by cycle, and step past the count for the late-winter earth-king day.

sentences.zh: 求次季土王日術曰：加大餘九十一、小餘五千二百四十四、小分六，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次季土王日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next season’s Earth King day says: Add great remainder 91, small remainder 5,244, and small fraction 6; when small fraction fills the small-fraction divisor, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the Obscuration divisor, carry to great remainder; when great remainder fills 60, remove it; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the next season’s Earth King day.
translations.idiomatic: Next season’s earth-king day: add great remainder 91, small remainder 5,244, and small fraction 6 with the usual carries, drop full sexagenary cycles, index, and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 推滅沒術曰：因冬至積沒有小餘者，加積沒一，以沒分乘之，以沒法八萬八千四百一十七除之，所得為積日，不盡為沒餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing extinction and submersion says: Where winter solstice accumulated submersion has a small remainder, add one to accumulated submersion; multiply by the submersion fraction; divide by the submersion divisor 88,417; what is obtained is accumulated days; what does not exhaust is submersion remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Extinction and submersion: if winter solstice leaves a submersion small remainder, increment accumulated submersion, multiply by the submersion fraction, and divide by submersion divisor 88,417 for accumulated days and submersion remainder.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為沒日，命以紀，算外，即所求天正十一月冬至後沒日。

translations.literal: Remove accumulated days by six tens; what does not exhaust is the submersion day; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the submersion day after winter solstice in civil-year November of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Remove sixties from accumulated days; the remainder is the submersion day—index by cycle and step past the count for the first submersion after November winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次滅術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘五萬七千二百四十四，沒餘滿沒法從沒日，沒日滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次沒日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next submersion says: Add submersion day 69 and submersion remainder 57,244; when submersion remainder fills the submersion divisor, carry to submersion day; when submersion day fills 60, remove it; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the next submersion day.
translations.idiomatic: Next submersion: add day 69 and remainder 57,244 with carry at the submersion divisor, drop full sexagenary cycles, index, and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 餘盡者為滅。

translations.literal: When the remainder is exhausted, it is extinction.
translations.idiomatic: A zero remainder marks extinction.

sentences.zh: 求次沒術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘一萬九百一十五、沒分六萬二千二百八十五，沒分滿沒法從沒餘，沒餘滿蔀法從沒日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next extinction says: Add submersion day 69, submersion remainder 19,915, and submersion fraction 62,285; when submersion fraction fills the submersion divisor, carry to submersion remainder; when submersion remainder fills the Obscuration divisor, carry to submersion day.
translations.idiomatic: Next extinction: add day 69, remainder 19,915, and fraction 62,285 with carries at the submersion and obscuration divisors.

sentences.zh: 命起前沒月，曆月大小除之，不滿月者，即後沒日及沒餘、沒分。

translations.literal: Count from the prior submersion month; eliminate by long and short months of the calendar; what does not fill a month: the later submersion day and submersion remainder and fraction.
translations.idiomatic: From the prior submersion month, walk long and short months; the fractional month yields the next submersion day, remainder, and fraction.

sentences.zh: 命曰如上，算外，即次沒日。

translations.literal: Count as above; outside the reckoning: the next submersion day.
translations.idiomatic: Index as before and step past the count for the next submersion day.

sentences.zh: 推四正卦術曰：因冬至大小餘即坎卦用事日，春分即震卦用事日，夏至即離卦用事日，秋分即兌卦用事日。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the four cardinal hexagrams says: From winter solstice great and small remainders take the Kan hexagram dominion day; at spring equinox the Zhen hexagram dominion day; at summer solstice the Li hexagram dominion day; at autumn equinox the Dui hexagram dominion day.
translations.idiomatic: Four cardinal hexagrams: winter solstice remainders give the Kan dominion day; spring equinox gives Zhen; summer solstice gives Li; autumn equinox gives Dui.

sentences.zh: 中孚因坎卦。

translations.literal: Zhong Fu derives from the Kan hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Fu follows the Kan hexagram.

sentences.zh: 求次卦術曰：加坎卦大餘六，小餘一千四百七十三、小分十四、微分四，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即復卦用事日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next hexagram says: Add to the Kan hexagram great remainder 6, small remainder 1,473, small fraction 14, and minute fraction 4; when minute fractions fill five, carry to small fraction; when small fraction fills the small-fraction divisor, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the Obscuration divisor, carry to great remainder; when great remainder fills 60, remove it; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: the Fu hexagram dominion day.
translations.idiomatic: Next hexagram: add to Kan great remainder 6, small remainder 1,473, small fraction 14, and minute fraction 4 with the usual carries, drop full sexagenary cycles, index, and step past the count for the Fu dominion day.

sentences.zh: 十一月，未濟、蹇、頤、中孚、復。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Wei Ji, Jian, Yi, Zhong Fu, Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Wei Ji, Jian, Yi, Zhong Fu, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，屯、謙、睽、升、臨。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Zhun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Zhun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, and Lin.

sentences.zh: 正月，小過、蒙、益、漸、泰。

translations.literal: First month: Xiao Guo, Meng, Yi, Jian, Tai.
translations.idiomatic: First month: Xiao Guo, Meng, Yi, Jian, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 二月，需、隨、晉、解、大壯。

translations.literal: Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, Da Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, and Da Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 三月，豫、訟、蠱、革、夬。

translations.literal: Third month: Yu, Song, Gu, Ge, Guai.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Yu, Song, Gu, Ge, and Guai.

sentences.zh: 四月，旅、師、比、小畜、乾。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiao Chu, Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiao Chu, and Qian.

sentences.zh: 五月，大有、家人、井、咸、姤。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Da You, Jia Ren, Jing, Xian, Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Da You, Jia Ren, Jing, Xian, and Gou.

sentences.zh: 六月，鼎、豐、渙、履、遯。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, and Dun.

sentences.zh: 七月，恒、節、同人、損、否。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tong Ren, Sun, Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tong Ren, Sun, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 八月，巽、萃、大畜、賁、觀。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Da Chu, Bi, Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Da Chu, Bi, and Guan.

sentences.zh: 九月，歸妹、无妄、明夷、困、剝。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Gui Mei, Wu Wang, Ming Yi, Kun, Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Gui Mei, Wu Wang, Ming Yi, Kun, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 十月，艮、既濟、噬嗑、大過、坤。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Gen, Ji Ji, Shi He, Da Guo, Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: Gen, Ji Ji, Shi He, Da Guo, and Kun.

sentences.zh: 四正為方伯，中孚為三公，復為天子，屯為諸侯，謙為大夫，睽為九卿，升還從三公，周而復始。

translations.literal: The four cardinals are regional lords; Zhong Fu is the Three Excellencies; Fu is the Son of Heaven; Zhun is the feudal lords; Qian is the grand masters; Kui is the Nine Ministers; Sheng returns following the Three Excellencies—cyclically beginning again.
translations.idiomatic: The four cardinal hexagrams map to regional lords; Zhong Fu to the Three Excellencies; Fu to the emperor; Zhun to feudal lords; Qian to grandees; Kui to the Nine Ministers; Sheng again follows the Three Excellencies in a repeating cycle.

sentences.zh: 九三應上九，清淨、微溫、陽風；

translations.literal: Nine in the third responding to nine on top: clear and pure, mildly warm, yang wind;
translations.idiomatic: When nine-three meets nine on top: clear air, mild warmth, and yang wind;

sentences.zh: 九三應上六，降赤、决溫、陰雨。

translations.literal: Nine in the third responding to six on top: descending red, decisive warmth, yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: When nine-three meets six on top: red haze, sudden warmth, and yin rain.

sentences.zh: 六三應上六，日澤、寒、陰雨；

translations.literal: [50] Six in the third responding to six on top: sun marsh, cold, yin rain;
translations.idiomatic: [50] When six-three meets six on top: marshy sun, cold, and yin rain;

sentences.zh: 六三應上九，麴塵、決寒、陽風。

translations.literal: [51] Six in the third responding to nine on top: flour-dust haze, decisive cold, yang wind.
translations.idiomatic: [51] When six-three meets nine on top: dusty haze, sharp cold, and yang wind.

sentences.zh: 諸卦上有陽爻者陽風，上有陰爻者陰雨。

translations.literal: Among the hexagrams, those with a yang line on top have yang wind; those with a yin line on top have yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: Hexagrams with yang in the upper line yield yang wind; those with yin above yield yin rain.

sentences.zh: 推七十二候術曰：因冬至大小餘即虎始交日，加大餘五、小餘一千二百二十八、微分一，微分滿三從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，依次候日。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the seventy-two hou says: From winter solstice great and small remainders take the day of tigers beginning to mate; add great remainder 5, small remainder 1,228, and minute fraction 1; when minute fractions fill three, carry to small fraction; when small fraction fills the small-fraction divisor, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the Obscuration divisor, carry to great remainder; when great remainder fills 60, remove it; count by cycle; outside the reckoning: each successive hou day in order.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two hou: from winter solstice remainders locate the “tigers begin mating” day; add great remainder 5, small remainder 1,228, and minute fraction 1 with the usual carries, drop full sexagenary cycles, index, and step past the count for each successive phenological hou.

sentences.zh: 冬至 虎始交 芸始生 荔挺生

translations.literal: Winter Solstice: tigers begin to mate; sinapis begins to grow; bricolea sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice — tigers begin mating; winter cress sprouts; bricolea shoots forth.

sentences.zh: 小寒 蚯蚓結 麋角解 水泉動

translations.literal: Minor Cold: earthworms coil; elk antlers shed; springs stir.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Cold — earthworms coil up; elk shed antlers; springs begin to move.

sentences.zh: 大寒 雁北向 鵲始巢 雉始雊

translations.literal: Major Cold: geese head north; magpies begin nesting; pheasants first crow.
translations.idiomatic: Major Cold — geese turn north; magpies start nests; pheasants first call.

sentences.zh: 立春 鷄始乳 東風解凍 蟄蟲始振

translations.literal: Start of Spring: hens begin brooding; east wind melts ice; hibernating insects stir.
translations.idiomatic: Start of Spring — hens brood; the east wind thaws ice; dormant insects awaken.

sentences.zh: 雨水 魚上負冰 獺祭魚 鴻雁來

translations.literal: Rain Water: fish rise under ice; otters offer fish; wild geese arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Rain Water — fish swim beneath ice; otters “sacrifice” fish; wild geese return.

sentences.zh: 驚蟄 始雨水 桃始華 倉庚鳴

translations.literal: Awakening of Insects: rain water begins; peaches bloom; orioles cry.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of Insects — rains begin; peach blossoms open; orioles sing.

sentences.zh: 春分 鷹化為鳩 玄鳥至 雷始發聲

translations.literal: Spring Equinox: hawks transform to turtledoves; dark birds arrive; thunder first sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Spring Equinox — hawks become turtledoves; swallows arrive; thunder first rolls.

sentences.zh: 清明 電始見 蟄蟲咸動 蟄蟲啟戶

translations.literal: Pure Brightness: lightning first appears; all hibernating insects move; hibernating insects open their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Brightness — lightning appears; dormant insects stir; they open their burrows.

sentences.zh: 穀雨 桐始華 田鼠化為鴽 虹始見

translations.literal: Grain Rain: paulownia blooms; field mice become quail; rainbows first appear.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain — paulownia flowers; field mice turn to quail; rainbows first show.

sentences.zh: 立夏 萍始生 戴勝降桑 螻蟈鳴

translations.literal: Start of Summer: duckweed sprouts; hoopoes descend to mulberry; frogs croak.
translations.idiomatic: Start of Summer — duckweed appears; hoopoes alight on mulberry; frogs begin calling.

sentences.zh: 小滿 蚯蚓出 王瓜生 苦菜秀

translations.literal: Minor Fullness: earthworms emerge; snake-gourd grows; bitter greens flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Fullness — earthworms surface; snake-gourd grows; bitter herbs flourish.

sentences.zh: 芒種 靡草死 小暑至 螗蜋生

translations.literal: Grain in Ear: delicate plants die; minor heat arrives; mantises hatch.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in Ear — tender grasses die; minor heat begins; mantises hatch.

sentences.zh: 夏至 鵙始鳴 反舌無聲 鹿角解

translations.literal: Summer Solstice: shrikes begin calling; mockingbirds fall silent; deer antlers shed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice — shrikes call; mockingbirds go quiet; deer shed antlers.

sentences.zh: 小暑 蟬始鳴 半夏生 木槿榮

translations.literal: Minor Heat: cicadas begin chirping; pinellia grows; hibiscus blooms.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Heat — cicadas chirp; pinellia grows; hibiscus flowers.

sentences.zh: 大暑 溫風至 蟋蟀居壁 鷹乃學習

translations.literal: Major Heat: warm winds arrive; crickets dwell in walls; hawks practice flying.
translations.idiomatic: Major Heat — warm winds blow; crickets move to walls; young hawks learn to fly.

sentences.zh: 立秋 腐草化為螢 土潤溽暑 涼風至

translations.literal: Start of Autumn: rotten grass becomes fireflies; earth moist, muggy heat; cool winds arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Start of Autumn — rotting grass turns to fireflies; earth grows damp and sultry; cool winds come.

sentences.zh: 處暑 白露降 寒蟬鳴 鷹祭鳥

translations.literal: Limit of Heat: white dew falls; cold cicadas chirp; hawks sacrifice birds.
translations.idiomatic: Limit of Heat — white dew descends; cold cicadas sing; hawks offer captured birds.

sentences.zh: 白露 天地始肅 暴風至 鴻雁來

translations.literal: White Dew: heaven and earth grow austere; violent winds arrive; wild geese arrive.
translations.idiomatic: White Dew — heaven and earth turn stern; gales blow; wild geese arrive.

sentences.zh: 秋分 玄鳥歸 羣鳥養羞 雷始收聲

translations.literal: Autumn Equinox: dark birds return; flocks nurture provisions; thunder withdraws.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Equinox — swallows depart; birds store food; thunder falls silent.

sentences.zh: 寒露 蟄蟲附戶 殺氣浸盛 陽氣日衰

translations.literal: Cold Dew: insects attach to doors; killing qi grows strong; yang qi daily declines.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Dew — insects shelter by doors; killing qi strengthens; yang qi wanes day by day.

sentences.zh: 霜降 水始涸 鴻雁來賓 雀入大水化為蛤

translations.literal: Frost Descent: waters begin to dry; guest wild geese arrive; sparrows enter great waters and become clams.
translations.idiomatic: Frost Descent — waters shrink; visiting geese arrive; sparrows dive into the floods and become clams.

sentences.zh: 立冬 菊有黃華 豺祭獸 水始冰

translations.literal: Start of Winter: chrysanthemums yellow; jackals sacrifice beasts; water begins to freeze.
translations.idiomatic: Start of Winter — chrysanthemums bloom yellow; jackals offer prey; water starts to freeze.

sentences.zh: 小雪 地始凍 雉入大水為蜃 虹藏不見

translations.literal: Minor Snow: earth begins to freeze; pheasants enter great waters and become oysters; rainbows hide away.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Snow — earth freezes; pheasants enter the waters as oysters; rainbows vanish.

sentences.zh: 大雪 冰益壯 地始坼 鶡旦不鳴[52]

translations.literal: Major Snow: ice grows stronger; earth begins to crack; crossbills cease calling at dawn[52]
translations.idiomatic: Major Snow — ice hardens; earth cracks; crossbills fall silent at dawn; see note 52.

sentences.zh: 推上朔術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以六律乘之，以六旬去之，不盡者命以甲子，算外，[53]即上朔日。

translations.literal: Method for pushing upper new moons says: Set [the count] from entering the cycle through the year sought in full, subtract one; multiply by the six pitch pipes; remove by six tens; what does not exhaust, count from jiazi; outside the reckoning, [53] that is the upper new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Upper new moon: set years since cycle entry minus one, multiply by six lü, remove sixties, index from jiazi, [53] and step past the count for the upper new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 推五星見伏術第七

translations.literal: Method for pushing the five planets' appearance and disappearance, Treatise 7.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 7: computing the five planets' apparitions and occultations.

sentences.zh: 上元甲子以來至今大魏興和二年，歲在庚申，積二十九萬三千九百九十七算。

translations.literal: From Upper Origin jiazi through the present Great Wei's Xinghe year 2, the year stationed at gengshen, accumulated reckonings 293,997.
translations.idiomatic: From Upper Origin jiazi to the present Great Wei Xinghe 2 (year gengshen), the accumulated count is 293,997.

sentences.zh: 木精曰歲星，其數六百七十二萬三千八百八十八。

translations.literal: The essence of Wood is called the Year Star; its number is 6,723,888.
translations.idiomatic: Wood's essence is Jupiter; its divisor is 6,723,888.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑，其數一千三百一十四萬九千八十三。

translations.literal: The essence of Fire is called Sparkling Deluder; its number is 13,149,083.
translations.idiomatic: Fire's essence is Mars; its divisor is 13,149,083.

sentences.zh: 土精曰鎮星，其數六百三十七萬四千六十一。

translations.literal: The essence of Earth is called Queller Star; its number is 6,374,061.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's essence is Saturn; its divisor is 6,374,061.

sentences.zh: 金精曰太白，其數九百八十四萬三千八百八十二。

translations.literal: The essence of Metal is called Great White; its number is 9,843,882.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's essence is Venus; its divisor is 9,843,882.

sentences.zh: 水精曰辰星，其數一百九十五萬三千七百一十六。

translations.literal: The essence of Water is called Chronogram Star; its number is 1,953,716.
translations.idiomatic: Water's essence is Mercury; its divisor is 1,953,716.

sentences.translationExclusionReason: Standalone source note marker or critical-apparatus residue with no corresponding English sentence.

sentences.zh: 推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，以周天乘之，為五星之實；

translations.literal: Method for pushing the five planets says: Set [the count] from Upper Origin through the year sought in full, subtract one; multiply by the circuit of heaven; this is the five planets' dividend;
translations.idiomatic: Five planets: set years since Upper Origin minus one, multiply by the circuit of heaven for the planetary dividend;

sentences.zh: 各以其數為法，除之，所得為積合，不盡為合餘。

translations.literal: for each, take its number as divisor and divide; what is obtained is accumulated conjunction; what does not exhaust is conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: divide each by its own constant for accumulated conjunction and conjunction remainder.

sentences.zh: 以合餘減法，餘為入歲度分。

translations.literal: Subtract conjunction remainder from the divisor; the remainder is the parts entered into yearly degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the remainder from the divisor to obtain the degree-fraction entered into the year.

sentences.zh: 以日度法約之，所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。

translations.literal: Reduce by the solar-degree divisor; what is obtained is the morning-or-evening conjunction degree tally and degree remainder after winter solstice in civil-year November of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by the solar-degree divisor for the dawn/dusk conjunction count and remainder after November winter solstice of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 其金、水，以一合日數及合餘減合度算及度餘，得一者為晨，無所得者為夕；

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, subtract one conjunction day-count and conjunction remainder from the conjunction degree tally and degree remainder; when one is obtained it is morning; when nothing is obtained it is evening;
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, subtract one synodic day-count and remainder from the conjunction tally; a positive result is morning, none is evening;

sentences.zh: 若度餘不足減者，減合度算一，加日度法乃減之。

translations.literal: if the degree remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the conjunction degree tally and add the solar-degree divisor before subtracting.
translations.idiomatic: borrow one from the conjunction tally and add the solar-degree divisor if the degree remainder is too small.

sentences.zh: 命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度及度餘。

translations.literal: Count starting twelve degrees before Ox; eliminate by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, outside the reckoning: the morning-or-evening conjunction degree and remainder after winter solstice in civil-year November of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Index from twelve degrees before Ox, walk the lodges, and step past the count for the dawn/dusk conjunction longitude and remainder after November winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 徑推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，如法算之。

translations.literal: Direct method for pushing the five planets says: Set [the count] from Upper Origin through the year sought in full, subtract one; calculate by the [planet's] divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortcut for the five planets: years since Upper Origin minus one, reckoned directly by each divisor.

sentences.zh: 合度餘滿日度法，加合度算一，合度算滿合終日數去之。

translations.literal: When conjunction degree remainder fills the solar-degree divisor, add one to the conjunction degree tally; when the conjunction degree tally fills the total conjunction day-count, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Carry one to the conjunction tally when degree remainder fills the solar-degree divisor; drop full synodic cycles from the tally.

sentences.zh: 亦以合終日餘減合度餘，[55]若不足減者，減合度算一，加周虛。

translations.literal: Also subtract total conjunction day-remainder from conjunction degree remainder, [55] and if insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the conjunction degree tally and add the circuit void.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract synodic day-remainder from degree remainder, [55] borrowing one tally and adding circuit void if needed.

sentences.zh: [56]所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。

translations.literal: [56] What is obtained is the morning-or-evening conjunction degree tally and degree remainder after winter solstice in civil-year November of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: [56] The result is the dawn/dusk conjunction tally and remainder after November winter solstice of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 其求金水及命度，[57]皆如上法。

translations.literal: In seeking Metal and Water and in counting degrees, [57] all follow the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Venus, Mercury, and lodge indexing all use the same method; see note 57.

sentences.zh: 求星合月及日術曰：置冬至去朔日數，減一，加合度算。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the star's conjunction month and day says: Set the days from winter solstice to new moon, subtract one, and add to the conjunction degree tally.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction month and day: add winter-solstice-to-new-moon days minus one to the conjunction tally.

sentences.zh: 冬至小餘以加合度餘，合度餘滿日度法去之，加合度算一。

translations.literal: Add winter solstice small remainder to conjunction degree remainder; when conjunction degree remainder fills the solar-degree divisor, remove it and add one to the conjunction degree tally.
translations.idiomatic: Add winter solstice small remainder to degree remainder, carrying to the tally when it fills the solar-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 合度算變成合日算，合度餘為日餘，命日起天正十一月，如曆月大小除之，不滿月者，算外，即星合月及日。

translations.literal: The conjunction degree tally becomes the conjunction day tally; conjunction degree remainder becomes day remainder; count days starting from civil-year November as in the calendar's long and short months; what does not fill a month, outside the reckoning: the star's conjunction month and day.
translations.idiomatic: Convert tally to day-count and remainder to day-fraction, walk months from November, and step past the count for the conjunction month and day.

sentences.zh: 有閏以閏計之。

translations.literal: When there is intercalation, account for it in the count.
translations.idiomatic: Include intercalary months in the reckoning.

sentences.zh: 求後合月及日術曰：以合終日數及合終日餘加前入月算及餘，餘滿日度法從日，[58]如曆月大小除之，起前合月，算外，即後合月及日。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the later conjunction month and day says: Add the total conjunction day-count and total conjunction day-remainder to the prior entered-month tally and remainder; when remainder fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to days, [58] eliminate by long and short months as in the calendar, starting from the prior conjunction month; outside the reckoning: the later conjunction month and day.
translations.idiomatic: Next conjunction: add synodic days and remainder to the prior month tally, carry at the solar-degree divisor, [58] walk long and short months from the prior conjunction, and step past the count.

sentences.zh: 其金、水以一合日數及合日餘加之，[59]加夕得晨，加晨得夕也。

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, add one conjunction day-count and conjunction day-remainder; [59] adding to evening yields morning; adding to morning yields evening.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, add one synodic day and remainder; [59] evening plus the increment gives morning, morning gives evening.

sentences.zh: 求後合度術曰：以行星度餘加前合度及度餘，度餘滿日度法從度，命起前合度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即後合度餘。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the later conjunction degree says: Add planetary degree remainder to the prior conjunction degree and degree remainder; when degree remainder fills the solar-degree divisor, carry to degrees; count starting from the prior conjunction degree; eliminate by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, outside the reckoning: the later conjunction degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Later conjunction longitude: add planetary motion to prior degree and remainder, carry, index from the prior conjunction, walk lodges, and step past the count for the remainder.

sentences.zh: 逕斗除其分，其分四千一百一十七。

translations.literal: Pass Dipper and remove its fraction; its fraction is 4,117.
translations.idiomatic: Deduct the Dipper shortcut fraction of 4,117.

sentences.zh: 歲星：合終日數三百九十八，合終日餘一萬二千六百八，周虛三千二百五十二，行星三十三度，度餘八千四百九十一。

translations.literal: Year Star: total conjunction day-count 398, total conjunction day-remainder 12,608, circuit void 3,252, planetary motion 33 degrees, degree remainder 8,491.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter: synodic days 398, day-remainder 12,608, circuit void 3,252, motion 33° with remainder 8,491.

translations.literal: Method for pacing the five stars through the ephemeris says: By the procedure's hidden-day degrees and remainder add the star-conjunction day-degrees and remainder; when the remainder fills the day-degree divisor 16,860 obtain one, carry from the whole and count as before, [72] obtaining the star's appearance day-degrees and remainder.
